parentQA.a: Jack first, then Ryan. Both have Eli's number, and there is no account manager or call center in between. We're a mid-size agency on purpose: he will not be represented in the shadow of a higher-profile client.

Agent fees on NFL playing contracts are capped by the NFLPA, and ours go in writing before anything is signed. Nothing is owed up front, and nothing is owed on money he never receives. We'll walk through the exact terms with you in person.

parentQA.q: How do you protect what he earns?
parentQA.a: Ryan writes the guarantee and injury language himself. Beyond the contract: we screen every financial advisor and money manager before he meets them, coordinate taxes, set up disability insurance, and build a budget in year one. The goal is a lifetime of financial security. A good first contract is only the start.

parentQA.q: What happens if he gets hurt?
parentQA.a: Injury settlements, grievances, and second medical opinions are ours to handle, and the disability policy is in place before the first snap. We've done this for players at every level of the roster.

parentQA.q: What if he's not drafted where we hope?
parentQA.a: We have placed undrafted free agents who are still in the league. The draft slot decides the first contract; preparation decides the second. ElevaTE exists to make year one count regardless of the round.

35 years. Combined 50 years of experience representing NFL players. Six clients who were the highest paid at their position. Jack played the position; Ryan is a licensed attorney. You can call any parent of a current client; we'll give you the numbers.

handle: Rookie deal, extensions, guarantees, fine appeals, grievances. Ryan writes the language.
Budget in year one. Every advisor and money manager screened before you meet them.
Multi-state filings coordinated. You sign; you don't chase.
Disability policy in place before the first snap. Second medical opinions on us to arrange.
Relocation, housing, car, travel. You land in a city with a place to live.
Interview prep, press, social. Nothing you say gets you in trouble.
Off-season plans, Nashville access, recovery. Every year, not just the draft.
Post-career benefits filed, planning done. The career ends; the security doesn't.
